data.title: Understanding U.S. Allies’ Current Legal Authority to Implement AI and Semiconductor Export Controls | CSIS
data.snippet: This paper provides an in-depth analysis of U.S. allies’ export control authorities related to AI and semiconductor technologies and does the same analysis for China. It demonstrates that U.S. allies often do not have equivalents to U.S. export control authorities and tools like the FDPR and Entity List, but that they generally do have the capability to introduce some controls on advanced semiconductor chips and related equipment not covered by multilateral export control regimes.

data.title: Understanding the Artificial Intelligence Diffusion Framework: Can Export Controls Create a U.S.-Led Global Artificial Intelligence Ecosystem? | RAND
data.snippet: This is the first comprehensive framework for managing global AI technology diffusion through export controls. 🇨🇳 China Now Proposes Export Controls on AI Models, Chips and Agents — Bloomberg 

Draft proposal covers 23 AI technologies, including large language models, agents, chip designs and computing clusters. Restricted technologies would include model weights and source code for products exceeding certain performance thresholds.

BREAKING: China just moved to put export controls on its own AI. The Commerce and Science ministries proposed adding 23 AI technologies, including large models, AI agents and computing clusters, to the country's restricted-export list (MOFCOM-MOST Notice No. 48, Oct 16; Reuters; Bloomberg).

- Model weights and source code above certain performance thresholds would be covered, along with chip designs, Bloomberg reports
- Tech already released as open source or published in academic papers is excluded, per the ministry notice
- Pre-export registration starts now: selling or licensing covered tech abroad, or a foreign entity taking control of its owner, must be registered with MOFCOM first
- Public comments run through Nov 15. The package also adds 5 biomedicine and 12 solar technologies
- The ministry calls it routine and says it targets no specific country

🚨 Breaking news on AI policy

China has proposed export controls on 23 AI technologies, including advanced model weights, agents and chip-design technology. Temporary pre-export registration for covered technology transfers takes effect immediately.

The draft covers specified technologies under technical, capability and data-related criteria. Model controls include weights, key checkpoints, source code, training optimization and inference acceleration.
→ AI technology already made public through open-source releases or academic papers is excluded
→ The commerce ministry says overseas API calls, app/web access and SaaS use fall outside the model-technology export scope
→ Overseas local deployment of restricted technology falls within scope; deployment on a company's own overseas cloud can qualify for automatic licensing

Public consultation on the revised export-control list runs through November 15.
